lines.speaker: bramm
lines.text: A fine pair of shoulders. Let us find out whether they carry anything. Six lengths of sound timber. Our rear axle will not mend itself.

lines.speaker: bramm
lines.text: Check your edge. Check your footing. Then check whether your mother has noticed you standing idle.

lines.speaker: bramm
lines.text: Bark torn above my shoulder. Blood on the needles. Something in Wolfscar Hollow has grown bold. Read its trail before you offer it your throat.

lines.speaker: bramm
lines.text: You brought meat home. Your mother is pretending not to be pleased. I shall pretend the same. Eat.

lines.speaker: bramm
lines.text: You came back for me. I will not spend the rest of my years thanking you. I will spend them making certain that choice was worth the trouble.

lines.speaker: svala
lines.text: Two cuts of meat, one length for the fire. Eat a portion yourself, then set one aside for Sava. We do not ask the hearth to keep us while feeding it nothing.

lines.speaker: svala
lines.text: Hungry? Of course you are. The interesting question is what you have brought me.

lines.speaker: svala
lines.text: Ash is poor building timber. We carry the living, the names, and the fire. Astrid kept the ember-pot. Do not let anyone call that a small thing.

lines.speaker: gorund
lines.text: These pines fed our grandsires. My axe has marked their bounds for two hundred winters. Let another chief come measure them against me.

lines.speaker: gorund
lines.text: Stonebelly asks for the crossing, the northern hunt, and our bowed heads. He may have the answer carried to him: Emberhide kneels only to lift its dead.

choices: I will take the northern trail after the feast.
There are people I wish to speak with first.

lines.speaker: dorrik
lines.text: Six lengths? I could carry a tree. Roots and all. Fetch six before that axle is mended and I owe you supper. Unless you intend to let your father carry you too.

choices: You owe me a meal if I do.

lines.speaker: dorrik
lines.text: I had a much finer boast prepared. Then the wolf looked at me. I am keeping the boast for something smaller.

lines.speaker: dorrik
lines.text: If anyone asks, the heavy end was mine.

lines.speaker: astrid
lines.text: Your father has you hauling timber? Good. I have been hauling pots since dawn. When you become a mighty lord, remember which work made supper appear.

lines.speaker: astrid
lines.text: Mother kept our little hearth pendant in the family coffer. I carried the living embers instead. The coffer is still at the Crossing. Bring it home, if home is to mean anything.

lines.speaker: astrid
lines.text: You even kept the broken clasp. Good. I can mend a clasp. Some things should not be replaced simply because the road became hard.

lines.speaker: astrid
lines.text: You remembered what mattered to me. That earns a place beside my fire. Whether it earns anything more is something we could discover.

choices: Your friendship is enough for me.

lines.speaker: svala
lines.text: First the hunters. Then those who worked. Dorrik, invent a third category and you can eat it.

lines.speaker: bramm
lines.text: Let the boy have the shoulder. He brought it back with his own hands.

lines.speaker: astrid
lines.text: A hunter at last. I shall have to find a new insult.

lines.speaker: gorund
lines.text: A rider brought Stonebelly's demand. Let him smell our feast while he waits for my answer.

lines.speaker: svala
lines.text: Smoke over the river. That is our canvas. Bramm is by the west wagon; Dorrik held the eastern path. I have Astrid. Go!

lines.speaker: hrothgar
lines.text: Gorund would not yield his hunting rights. A great chief. A great mistake. This torc is all the answer his household will receive.

lines.speaker: hrothgar
lines.text: And you. Still standing, still swinging. Come, then. Show me what his hearth raised.

lines.speaker: hrothgar
lines.text: Enough. A lesser creature would have begged before the second blow.

lines.speaker: hrothgar
lines.text: I have broken your chief, not your usefulness. Bring your living kin. Eat at my fire. Earn the next thing you call your own.

choices: I will carry our fire onward.

lines.speaker: hrothgar
lines.text: Ha! Blood in my beard, my knees in the mud. I will remember that. So will every witness here.

lines.speaker: hrothgar
lines.text: Your chief is dead and my host holds the crossing. But your strength has bought terms. Bring your kin as my guests, and no man shall call you spoil.

choices: My kin come under my protection.

lines.speaker: thyra
lines.text: Count the wagons before you speak of a great household. Each mouth is a promise someone must keep.

lines.speaker: thyra
lines.text: Your people have places by the southern fires. Find me when you have looked about. We will discuss what your hands can earn.

lines.speaker: hrothgar
lines.text: A wolf takes a valley because it can hold it. A chief must also feed everyone who follows him into it. Do something useful today. Surprise me.

lines.speaker: hrothgar
lines.text: A wagon, a fire, stores enough to refuse a bad bargain. Now you begin to understand power. Keep earning it.

lines.speaker: thyra
lines.text: Hunt, hammer iron, carry timber, take paid blows. I care little which. I care that your supper costs my household less than your work brings it.

choices: I will find work with Runa.

lines.speaker: thyra
lines.text: A household can survive an enemy. Wasteful friends are another matter.

lines.speaker: runa
lines.text: The Sundered Pass is choked with stone. Three falls across the road. Break them down; keep the ore. Something young and hungry has been licking the exposed seam.

lines.speaker: runa
lines.text: That stone-eater will pull half a hillside if the traces fit. Two hides, two sound lengths. Make a harness that does not bite its shoulders.

lines.speaker: runa
lines.text: See? It leans into the traces instead of fighting them. You watched the beast. Most men only watch themselves. I like that.

lines.speaker: runa
lines.text: Walk with me after the beasts are settled. You can tell me whether that competent pair of hands belongs to a man I should know better.

lines.speaker: eydis
lines.text: Blackstone wants three goblin raiders removed from the Cairn. Thirty coin. They asked for a smaller price. I suggested a smaller warrior.

choices: Forty. I will add two cuts of meat.

lines.speaker: eydis
lines.text: Three raiders at Goblin Cairn. A bargain is not a song: it needs an ending before I pay for it.

lines.speaker: eydis
lines.text: The watchmen saw the Cairn empty. I trust frightened watchmen more than confident hunters. Shall we settle?

lines.speaker: eydis
lines.text: Coin as promised. If you want a household, I can put a wagon beneath it. Eight timber, two hides, twenty-five coin. A fair beginning, with room to grow.

lines.speaker: eydis
lines.text: Eight timber, two hides, twenty-five coin. The wagon has a stout axle and room for a sleeping platform. The household you put inside is your affair.

lines.speaker: eydis
lines.text: Three ore and two timber. Help me finish a commission and I will hone that hunting axe properly. A sharp edge is cheaper than a dead customer.

lines.speaker: eydis
lines.text: A clean edge and an honest day's work. Your axe will bite deeper now. I could do business with someone who finishes what he begins.

lines.speaker: eydis
lines.text: You kept your bargain. You have work worth doing. If you wish to speak of a future together, bring the same care to that conversation.

choices: Let us remain friends and partners in work.

lines.speaker: svala
lines.text: A small fire. That is how they all begin. Feed it. Make room for those you choose.

lines.speaker: hrothgar
lines.text: Your hearth, young Emberhide. Stay with my host or take the road. What you build next is yours to answer for.

lines.speaker: eydis
lines.text: Meat for the pot, hides for the purse. Blackstone measures everything twice when an Ogre is watching.
